source.author: Anastasia Kireeva
source.title: Low-degree hardness of finding the largest clique in Erdős–Rényi graph (problems 36-38)
source.target: source-valid conditions on (P_n,Q_n) under which bounded low-degree advantage through D=(log n)^{1+Omega(1)} rigorously implies polynomial/noisy indistinguishability

method_outcomes.B3: Proved an arbitrary-many-parity collective low-degree theorem for any finite ferromagnetic Ising tree. The bound is expressed through a robust tree T-join erasure spectrum B_k(C;rho,T), using an exact degree-preserving Markov innovation basis.
method_outcomes.B28: Replaced hard minimum distance by a spectral-escape criterion. Bounded low-degree spectral mass may include exceptional low-support irreps/codewords provided their support escapes every fixed cutoff and the noise-discounted high tail vanishes.
method_outcomes.B17: Transferred classical expander/LDPC/group-code weight-spectrum bounds into explicit noisy-indistinguishability sufficient conditions. No new coding theorem is claimed; coding results remain prior art.

new_claims.robust_distance_corollary: If delta_D^T(c)>=L for every nonzero c in C, then Adv^{<=D} <= sqrt(D)(e n C_rho^2/D)^{D/2} 2^M rho^L (conservative).
new_claims.spectral_escape: If sum_{k<=D_n}A_{n,k}=O(1), every fixed-support prefix mass tends to zero, and sum_{k>D_n}A_{n,k}e^{-2tk}->0, then source LDA is bounded and noisy chi-square/TV tend to zero.
new_claims.coding_transfer: For code dimension M_n and distance d_n, chi2 after coordinate refresh at t is <= exp(M_n log 2 - 2t d_n); full spectral-shape bounds sharpen this via sup_omega(g(omega)-2t omega).

classical_or_close_tools: regular LDPC and D-GLDPC weight spectra
tree-Ising bond variables and Markov innovations

remaining_obligation: Extend the many-parity tree theorem to loopy bounded-degree weak-Ising/Gibbs phases using high-temperature/current/polymer control without a full monomial entropy loss.
Certify interior discounted spectrum directly for the many-parity Ising-tree model, ideally by an exact two-copy tree transfer/code enumerator.
Allow slowly growing low-spectrum mass through a quantitative posterior/large-deviation profile rather than O(1) mass only.
Control the polylogarithmic small-weight spectrum of concrete Tanner/LDPC families uniformly through D_n=(log n)^{1+Omega(1)}.
Obtain an actual low-support representation-spectrum bound for nonabelian group-code families.
Translate Hsieh regularization and Chen-Li reassembly into spectral-escape/interior-pressure conditions without false subsumption.
Quantify Mao as a lower obstruction on discounted spectral mass under aligned noise.
Obtain actual P26 plus one distinct OTHER full theorem/source audit before closure.
